page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the Tau T2D machine family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 8 dedicated physical cores with 8 vCPUs, operating at a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. It is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the t2d-standard-8 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested systems via stress-ng. Multi-core performance, however, falls within the average range for both stress-ng and Geekbench tests. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only and write operations on large uncached blocks, consistently register in the average tier, with read speeds at 95.12 GB/sec and write speeds at 51.75 GB/sec. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware-accelerated instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio and dedicated core allocation, the t2d-standard-8 is designed for general-purpose workloads. It is suited for web serving, application hosting, and database operations, as reflected in its average database and Redis SET benchmark results. The absence of local storage means workloads must rely on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff to consider for I/O-intensive applications.
